name: Ansys HFSS (Ansys Electronics Desktop)
description: HFSS is Ansys' 3D full-wave electromagnetic field solver for high-frequency components: antennas and arrays, RF and microwave passives, filters, connectors, packages, PCB signal integrity, waveguides, radomes and EMI/EMC problems. It lives inside Ansys Electronics Desktop (AEDT), the common shell that also hosts HFSS 3D Layout, Maxwell, Q3D Extractor, Icepak, Circuit (Nexxim), Twin Builder and EMIT, so a 3D model, a layout database and a circuit schematic can be dynamically linked in one project. A design is built in the 3D Modeler from primitives and booleans or imported from CAD, materials are assigned, boundaries and excitations (wave ports, lumped ports, radiation, Floquet, plane waves) define the electromagnetic problem, and an adaptive finite-element solver refines the mesh until the S-parameters converge. Solution types cover Driven Modal and Driven Terminal frequency-domain FEM, Eigenmode, Transient (time domain), Characteristic Mode, and the asymptotic SBR+ ray solver for electrically huge scenes, with hybrid FEM-IE and PO regions in between. Results come back as S/Y/Z parameters, Touchstone files, far-field radiation patterns and antenna parameters, and field overlays that can be post-processed in the Fields Calculator; Optimetrics adds parametric sweeps, optimisation, sensitivity and statistical analysis on top.

automation.summary: AEDT records and replays its own scripting language. Tools > Record Script To File captures every GUI action as IronPython or VBScript against the AEDT scripting object model, and Tools > Run Script replays it, which makes recording the fastest way to discover the exact call and argument array for any dialog. The object model is a small hierarchy of automation objects: oDesktop (the application), oProject, oDesign, oEditor (obtained with oDesign.SetActiveEditor("3D Modeler")) and a set of modules obtained with oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup"), ("MeshSetup"), ("AnalysisSetup"), ("ReportSetup"), ("Optimetrics"), ("RadField"), ("FieldsReporter") and ("Solutions"). Almost every method takes a nested array of name/value pairs mirroring the dialog it replaces. Scripts run from the GUI or headless from the command line: `ansysedt -RunScriptAndExit script.py` executes and closes, `-RunScript` executes and leaves the session open, `-ng` suppresses the GUI, `-BatchSolve` solves a named or all setups in a project, and `-batchoptions` overrides registry/solve options such as core counts and distributed machine lists for a single run. PyAEDT (the ansys.aedt.core Python package) is the modern, supported wrapper: it launches or attaches to a desktop session, exposes pythonic classes such as Hfss, Hfss3dLayout, Maxwell3d, Q3d, Icepak and Circuit, and wraps the raw object model with named arguments, object handles and helper workflows while still leaving the underlying COM objects reachable. For solving at scale, AEDT supports HPC licensing with multiple cores, distributed and spectral/domain decomposition, GPU acceleration, Remote Simulation Manager (RSM) and submission to LSF, PBS, SLURM and Windows HPC schedulers.

cli.description: Run a script with no graphical interface and exit when the script finishes. This is the standard headless entry point for model generation and post-processing. Use -RunScript instead if the session should stay open after the script completes.

Pass arguments into the script. The values are read inside the script from the ScriptArgument environment/desktop property (for example ScriptArgument in IronPython, or sys.argv in a CPython script launched through PyAEDT), so one script can serve many parameter sets.

Solve a project headless. -BatchSolve with no setup name solves every design and setup in the project; append Setup1:Sweep1 style qualifiers to restrict it. -Distributed plus -machinelist spreads the job over several machines, and -auto lets AEDT choose the distribution strategy.
Solve one named design and setup rather than the whole project. The qualifier takes the form DesignName:VariationOrNominal:SetupName; use it in queue scripts so each scheduler job owns one setup.

Override registry-backed solve options for a single run without changing the saved preferences. Options are given as quoted 'path/Key'=value pairs, or collected in an options file referenced by -batchoptions filename.

Run a batch extraction job described by an options file, used by the layout and parasitic-extraction workflows (SIwave-style extraction and Q3D/2D Extractor runs) to produce models without opening the interface.
Enable beta features for the session so scripts can reach options that are still pre-release. Also useful when a recorded script was captured on a machine that had beta features switched on.
Name the project, design and setup explicitly instead of encoding them in the batch-solve qualifier. Handy when a wrapper script builds the command line from scheduler variables.

Solve headless while writing progress to the console so a scheduler log shows adaptive-pass and sweep progress. On Linux always launch through the ansysedt wrapper script in v251/AnsysEM rather than calling the executable directly, because the wrapper sets up the required environment.

apis.name: AEDT scripting object model (IronPython / CPython / VBScript)
apis.description: The native automation interface that the GUI itself drives. A handful of objects form the hierarchy: oDesktop for application and project management, oProject for designs and saving, oDesign for modules and analysis, oEditor for geometry, and modules retrieved by name with oDesign.GetModule(...). Most methods take a nested array of alternating property names and values that mirrors the dialog being replaced, so the reliable way to write one is Tools > Record Script To File, perform the action in the GUI, then edit the recorded call. The same script text runs in the embedded IronPython engine, in CPython through PyAEDT, or as VBScript.
apis.example:
import ScriptEnv
ScriptEnv.Initialize("Ansoft.ElectronicsDesktop")
oDesktop.RestoreWindow()
oProject = oDesktop.NewProject()
oProject.InsertDesign("HFSS", "Patch", "DrivenModal", "")
oDesign = oProject.SetActiveDesign("Patch")
oEditor = oDesign.SetActiveEditor("3D Modeler")

oEditor.CreateBox(
    ["NAME:BoxParameters",
     "XPosition:=", "-20mm", "YPosition:=", "-20mm", "ZPosition:=", "0mm",
     "XSize:=", "40mm", "YSize:=", "40mm", "ZSize:=", "1.575mm"],
    ["NAME:Attributes",
     "Name:=", "Sub", "MaterialValue:=", "\"Rogers RT/duroid 5880 (tm)\"",
     "SolveInside:=", True])

oModule = oDesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
oModule.AssignPerfectE(["NAME:PerfE1", "Objects:=", ["Ground"], "InfGroundPlane:=", False])

oModule = oDesign.GetModule("AnalysisSetup")
oModule.InsertSetup("HfssDriven",
    ["NAME:Setup1", "Frequency:=", "2.45GHz", "MaxDeltaS:=", 0.02, "MaximumPasses:=", 12])
oModule.InsertFrequencySweep("Setup1",
    ["NAME:Sweep1", "IsEnabled:=", True, "Type:=", "Interpolating",
     "RangeType:=", "LinearCount", "RangeStart:=", "2GHz", "RangeEnd:=", "3GHz",
     "RangeCount:=", 401, "SaveFields:=", False])

oDesign.Analyze("Setup1")
oProject.SaveAs("C:/work/patch.aedt", True)

apis.name: PyAEDT (ansys.aedt.core)
apis.description: Ansys' open-source Python client for AEDT, installed with `pip install pyaedt`. It launches or attaches to a desktop session, opens or creates projects and designs, and gives each application a class (Hfss, Hfss3dLayout, Maxwell3d, Maxwell2d, Q3d, Q2d, Icepak, Circuit, Mechanical, Emit) whose properties expose the modeler, boundaries, mesh, setups, variable manager, materials, Optimetrics and post-processor as ordinary Python objects. It hides the nested-array calling convention, returns object handles you can keep, and adds workflows such as automatic port creation, field plots and report export. The raw objects (hfss.odesign, hfss.oeditor, hfss.modeler.oeditor) remain available for anything not yet wrapped.
apis.example:
from ansys.aedt.core import Hfss

hfss = Hfss(version="2025.1", solution_type="Modal", non_graphical=True, new_desktop=True)
hfss["patch_w"] = "38mm"
hfss["patch_l"] = "29mm"

sub = hfss.modeler.create_box([-25, -25, 0], [50, 50, 1.575],
                              name="Sub", material="Rogers RT/duroid 5880 (tm)")
patch = hfss.modeler.create_rectangle("XY", ["-patch_w/2", "-patch_l/2", "1.575mm"],
                                      ["patch_w", "patch_l"], name="Patch")
hfss.assign_perfect_e([patch.name])
hfss.create_open_region(frequency="2.45GHz")

port = hfss.lumped_port(assignment="FeedSheet", integration_line=hfss.AxisDir.XPos,
                        impedance=50, name="P1")

setup = hfss.create_setup("Setup1")
setup.props["Frequency"] = "2.45GHz"
setup.props["MaximumPasses"] = 12
setup.update()
hfss.create_linear_count_sweep(setup="Setup1", units="GHz", start_frequency=2,
                               stop_frequency=3, num_of_freq_points=401,
                               sweep_type="Interpolating")
hfss.analyze()

hfss.insert_infinite_sphere(name="3D")
data = hfss.post.get_solution_data(expressions="dB(S(P1,P1))")
hfss.post.create_report("dB(S(P1,P1))")
hfss.export_touchstone(output_file=r"C:\work\patch.s1p")
hfss.save_project()
hfss.release_desktop()

apis.name: Record Script To File / Run Script
apis.description: The discovery mechanism for the whole object model. Tools > Record Script To File starts capturing; every subsequent GUI action is written as a scripting call with the exact module name and argument array; Tools > Stop Script Recording ends it. Tools > Run Script (or the Scripts ribbon) replays a .py or .vbs file. Because argument arrays are long and version-sensitive, recording first and editing second is far more reliable than writing calls from memory, and it is the recommended way to script a dialog that PyAEDT does not yet wrap.
apis.example:
# Workflow
# 1. Tools > Record Script To File...  -> save as assign_port.py
# 2. Perform the action in the GUI (e.g. assign a wave port with an integration line)
# 3. Tools > Stop Script Recording
# 4. Edit the recorded file, parameterise names, then Tools > Run Script

# In PyAEDT the equivalent raw call is still reachable:
oModule = hfss.odesign.GetModule("BoundarySetup")
oModule.AssignWavePort(["NAME:P1", "Objects:=", ["PortSheet"], "NumModes:=", 1,
                        "RenormalizeAllTerminals:=", True, "DoDeembed:=", False,
                        ["NAME:Modes", ["NAME:Mode1", "ModeNum:=", 1,
                         "UseIntLine:=", False]]])

apis.name: Optimetrics and design of experiments
apis.description: Optimetrics wraps the solver in parametric sweeps, optimisation, sensitivity, statistical and tuning studies driven by design variables. Setups are created from the GUI (Optimetrics > Add > Parametric / Optimization / Sensitivity / Statistical), from the object model through oDesign.GetModule("Optimetrics").InsertSetup, or in PyAEDT with hfss.parametrics.add and hfss.optimizations.add. Optimisers include Quasi Newton, Pattern Search, Sequential Non-linear Programming, Genetic Algorithm and MATLAB-linked optimisers, and cost functions are built from report expressions. For larger design-space exploration the project can be driven from Ansys optiSLang or Workbench DesignXplorer instead.
apis.example:
from ansys.aedt.core import Hfss
hfss = Hfss(version="2025.1", non_graphical=True)
hfss["patch_l"] = "29mm"

param = hfss.parametrics.add("patch_l", start_point="27mm", end_point="31mm",
                             step="0.5mm", variation_type="LinearStep")
param.add_calculation(calculation="dB(S(1,1))", ranges={"Freq": "2.45GHz"})

opt = hfss.optimizations.add(calculation="dB(S(1,1))", ranges={"Freq": "2.45GHz"},
                             optimization_type="Optimization")
opt.props["Goals"][0]["Condition"] = "<="
hfss.analyze_setup(param.name)

apis.name: HPC, distributed solve and job schedulers
apis.description: Solve resources are configured in Tools > Options > HPC and Analysis Options, where an Analysis Configuration sets cores, RAM limit, GPU acceleration and how many tasks run in parallel; a Distributed configuration spreads frequency points, domains or parametric variations over several machines. The same settings can be forced per run with -batchoptions on the command line. Remote Simulation Manager (RSM) lets a workstation dispatch jobs to a solve server, and the Submit Job dialog integrates with LSF, PBS Pro, SLURM, UGE and Windows HPC so an AEDT project can be queued from the interface or from a scheduler script that calls ansysedt -ng -BatchSolve.

apis.name: PyEDB and 3D Layout automation
apis.description: Layout-centric designs (PCBs, packages, IC interposers) are held in an Electronics Database (.aedb) rather than a 3D history tree. PyEDB (`pip install pyedb`) opens an .aedb directly, with or without a running AEDT session, to read and edit stackups, nets, padstacks, components, ports and simulation setups, and the Hfss3dLayout class in PyAEDT drives the 3D Layout solver on top of it. Boards enter through ODB++, IPC-2581, BRD, GDSII or AEDB import, and the Phi mesher and HFSS Region features control how much of the board is solved with full-wave accuracy.
apis.example:
from pyedb import Edb
edb = Edb(edbpath=r"C:\work\board.aedb", edbversion="2025.1")
print(edb.nets.netlist[:10])
edb.stackup.add_layer("L5", "L4", layer_type="signal", thickness="0.035mm")
edb.components.create_port_on_component("U1", net_list=["DDR_DQ0"], port_type="coax")
edb.save_edb()
edb.close_edb()

from ansys.aedt.core import Hfss3dLayout
h3d = Hfss3dLayout(project=r"C:\work\board.aedb", version="2025.1", non_graphical=True)
setup = h3d.create_setup("SIwaveSetup")
h3d.analyze()
h3d.export_touchstone(output_file=r"C:\work\board.s4p")

file_formats.description: Ansys Electronics Desktop project file: a text container holding every design in the project (HFSS, 3D Layout, Circuit, Maxwell, Icepak, Q3D), their geometry, materials, boundaries, setups, variables and report definitions. Opened with oDesktop.OpenProject or the PyAEDT application constructors.

Companion results folder written next to the .aedt file, containing meshes, solved field data, matrix data and profiles for every solved variation. Deleting it discards solutions but keeps the model; it is what makes a solved project directory so large.
Archived project: the .aedt file plus selected results, mesh and external files zipped into one portable archive with File > Archive. The usual way to hand a case to support or a colleague.

Electronics Database folder used by HFSS 3D Layout, SIwave and PyEDB for layout designs. Holds the stackup, nets, padstacks, components and layout geometry imported from ODB++, IPC-2581, BRD or GDSII.
Legacy standalone HFSS project file from releases before the Electronics Desktop unification (HFSS v15 and earlier). Modern AEDT can read it and convert the design into an .aedt project.

Touchstone network data (.s1p, .s2p, .s4p, ...) exported from the solution with HFSS > Results > Solution Data > Export Matrix Data, oModule('Solutions').ExportNetworkData or hfss.export_touchstone. The standard way to move S-parameters into a circuit simulator.

Scripting files for the AEDT object model. Recorded with Tools > Record Script To File, replayed with Tools > Run Script or ansysedt -RunScriptAndExit. PyAEDT scripts are ordinary CPython .py files run outside the desktop.

Neutral CAD geometry read by Modeler > Import and written by Modeler > Export: STEP, IGES, ACIS SAT and Parasolid. Native readers also exist for Creo, SolidWorks, Inventor, CATIA and NX when the corresponding translator is licensed.

2D layer-based geometry imports. DXF/DWG bring in planar outlines that can be thickened into 3D, and GDSII streams IC layout into HFSS 3D Layout or the 3D modeler through the technology-file mapping dialog.

3D component file: a self-contained modelling assembly with its geometry, materials, boundaries, excitations and mesh operations, optionally encrypted so it can be distributed without exposing the design. Created with Modeler > Create 3D Component and placed with Insert 3D Component.

Result export formats: CSV/TAB for report traces and tables, .fld for field data written on a grid or geometry by the Fields Calculator, and .ffd far-field data used by the antenna post-processing and array tools.

Ansys material library file. Custom materials added through Tools > Edit Libraries > Materials or oDefinitionManager.AddMaterial can be exported to a personal or shared .amat library for reuse across projects.

Solver log and profile data shown in the Solution Data window's Profile and Convergence tabs. In headless runs the console output from -monitor plus these files are the main way to see why a solve stalled or ran out of memory.
